mu-4133a9b8.stem: Which spinal segment does the biceps tendon reflex mainly test?
mu-4133a9b8.explanation: The biceps reflex runs through the musculocutaneous nerve and tests C5–C6, especially C5. The brachioradialis reflex is for C6, the triceps reflex for C7.

mu-ef6cce8c.stem: Which of the following muscles is NOT in the anterior compartment of the leg?
mu-ef6cce8c.explanation: The anterior compartment contains tibialis anterior, EHL, EDL and fibularis tertius, supplied by the deep fibular nerve. Fibularis brevis is in the lateral compartment (superficial fibular nerve).

mu-7996df31.stem: Where do the two heads of gastrocnemius arise?
options: From the posterior surfaces of the tibia and fibula
From the posterior surfaces of the medial and lateral femoral condyles
From the patella and patellar ligament
mu-7996df31.explanation: Because gastrocnemius arises from the femoral condyles it also crosses the knee and helps flex it. Soleus arises from the tibia and fibula and does not cross the knee.

mu-d1e6dcde.explanation: Popliteus is the muscle in the floor of the popliteal fossa; it unlocks the knee from full extension and is supplied by the tibial nerve.

mu-3811c4d1.stem: Which muscles are in the first (most superficial) layer of the sole of the foot?
options: Extensor digitorum brevis and extensor hallucis brevis
Abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis and abductor digiti minimi
Flexor hallucis brevis and adductor hallucis
mu-3811c4d1.explanation: The plantar muscles form four layers: 1. abductor hallucis, FDB, abductor digiti minimi; 2. quadratus plantae, lumbricals; 3. FHB, adductor hallucis, FDMB; 4. interossei.

mu-cb57c01f.stem: A basketball player landing from a jump reports pain at the front of the knee and cannot actively extend it; the patella lies higher than normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mu-cb57c01f.explanation: When the patellar ligament ruptures, quadriceps pulls the patella upwards (patella alta) and, with the extensor mechanism disrupted, the knee cannot be actively extended. In a quadriceps tendon rupture the patella stays low (patella baja).

mu-e59cf28c.stem: Which is the only palatal muscle supplied by the mandibular nerve (V3)?
mu-e59cf28c.explanation: All palatal muscles are supplied by the vagus through the pharyngeal plexus; the only exception is tensor veli palatini, derived from the 1st arch (V3). Tensor tympani is likewise supplied by V3.

mu-6fb5ef1a.stem: Which option gives the innervation of the middle ear muscles correctly?
options: Tensor tympani – mandibular nerve (V3); stapedius – facial nerve (VII)
mu-6fb5ef1a.explanation: Tensor tympani derives from the 1st arch (V3), stapedius from the 2nd arch (VII). Facial nerve lesions proximal to the nerve to stapedius cause hyperacusis.

mu-568138c7.stem: From which vertebrae does the right crus of the diaphragm arise?
mu-568138c7.explanation: The right crus arises from the bodies of L1–L3, the shorter left crus from L1–L2. Fibres of the right crus encircle the oesophagus like a sling to form the oesophageal hiatus.

mu-2b4b7a06.stem: What are the most common type and site of congenital diaphragmatic hernia?
options: Morgagni hernia – anteromedial, mostly on the right
Bochdalek hernia – anteromedial, mostly on the right
Bochdalek hernia – posterolateral, mostly on the left
Morgagni hernia – posterolateral, on the left
mu-2b4b7a06.explanation: A Bochdalek hernia forms posterolaterally (most often on the left) when the pleuroperitoneal membrane fails to close, causing lung hypoplasia in the newborn. A Morgagni hernia is rarer and anteromedial.

mu-64e5a84c.stem: What is the typical arm position in Erb–Duchenne palsy (upper trunk, C5–C6)?
options: Arm normal, only thumb opposition lost
Arm adducted and medially rotated, forearm extended and pronated ('waiter's tip')
Arm abducted and laterally rotated, forearm flexed
mu-64e5a84c.explanation: In C5–C6 injury deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus, biceps and brachialis are paralysed; the arm hangs adducted and medially rotated, the forearm extended and pronated. It results from birth trauma and forced widening of the shoulder–neck angle.

mu-0fe418f7.stem: Which muscles are most affected in Klumpke palsy (lower trunk, C8–T1)?
mu-0fe418f7.explanation: Injury of the C8–T1 roots (traction of the arm in excessive abduction) affects all intrinsic hand muscles and produces a claw hand; if T1 sympathetic fibres are involved, Horner syndrome may accompany it.

mu-4c3ad44c.stem: When the radial nerve is injured in a fracture of the middle third of the humerus, why is triceps brachii usually spared?
options: The branches to triceps leave before the nerve enters the spiral groove.
Triceps is supplied by the axillary nerve.
Triceps is supplied by the ulnar nerve.
The nerve does not pass through triceps in the spiral groove.
mu-4c3ad44c.explanation: In the upper arm, before entering the radial groove, the radial nerve gives its branches to the long and medial heads of triceps. In a mid-shaft fracture elbow extension is therefore mostly preserved, while wrist drop develops.

mu-06305979.stem: A rugby player whose finger was forcibly extended while grabbing an opponent's jersey cannot actively flex the DIP joint (jersey finger). Which tendon has ruptured?
options: Terminal part of the extensor tendon
mu-06305979.explanation: In jersey finger the FDP tendon avulses from the base of the distal phalanx; the ring finger is most often affected. Because only FDP flexes the DIP joint, this movement is lost.

options: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve
mu-fd7114cd.explanation: Quadratus femoris and gemellus inferior are supplied by the nerve to quadratus femoris from the sacral plexus. Obturator internus and gemellus superior are supplied by the nerve to obturator internus.

mu-5f7018d9.stem: Which muscles form the floor of the femoral triangle?
mu-5f7018d9.explanation: From lateral to medial the floor of the femoral triangle is formed by iliopsoas, pectineus and adductor longus; its roof is the fascia lata and cribriform fascia.

mu-617924a3.stem: Which hamstring muscle tears most often in sprinters?
mu-617924a3.explanation: The long head of biceps femoris is the most frequently injured hamstring because it is overstretched eccentrically at the end of the swing phase of running.

mu-ea64d105.stem: What is the function of quadratus plantae?
options: Correcting the oblique pull of the FDL tendon so the toes flex straight
mu-ea64d105.explanation: Quadratus plantae runs from the calcaneus to the lateral border of the FDL tendon; it corrects FDL's oblique pull from behind the medial malleolus so that the toes flex straight. It is supplied by the lateral plantar nerve.

mu-e51f982b.stem: After total hip replacement a patient cannot lift the foot (foot drop) and has numbness on the outer side of the leg. What is the most likely damage?
options: Injury of the fibular division of the sciatic nerve
mu-e51f982b.explanation: In hip surgery the fibular division of the sciatic nerve, more superficial and protected by less connective tissue, is injured more often; dorsiflexion and eversion are lost, with sensory loss on the outer leg.
